steve-gibson.text: Gibson (board president, elected 2022) said: "My goal is to make sure PCC works for everyone: the recent graduate, the working parent, the neighbor retraining for a new career." Per his campaign, his record includes PCC Northwest at John Muir High School, expanded workforce training and accessibility.

source.title: Pasadena Now: Steve Gibson seeks second term on Pasadena City College board (July 2026)

steve-gibson.text: Per his campaign, as a trustee Gibson supported fire-recovery training programs, including a new construction trades lab and expanded fire academy, electrical technology, welding and construction inspection programs.

source.title: Pasadena Now: Steve Gibson seeks second term on Pasadena City College board (July 2026)

steve-gibson.text: Endorsed by the PCC Faculty Association, per his campaign announcement.

source.title: Pasadena Now: Steve Gibson seeks second term on Pasadena City College board (July 2026)

steve-gibson.text: (2024) Gibson wrote that a trustee's role is to "ask tough questions and ensure accountability to our communities, especially our communities of color," and that graduation rates for Latino and Black students remain stagnant.

source.title: Pasadena Now: Guest Opinion: Steve Gibson, Why I support James Aragon for PCC Trustee (Mar 2024)

steve-gibson.text: Campaign site: on the board, Gibson "introduced and championed a policy to decarbonize Pasadena City College."

source.title: Steve Gibson for Pasadena City College (campaign site)

steve-gibson.text: In an Aug. 2025 column after losing his Altadena home in the Eaton Fire, Gibson urged the EPA to "uphold the Endangerment Finding" and called proposed climate rollbacks "a catastrophic step backward."

source.title: Pasadena Now: Guest Opinion: PCC Trustee Steve Gibson, From Altadena to Washington: When Climate Change Hits Home, We Must Act (Aug. 2025)

steve-gibson.text: (2022) Wrote that PCC part-time faculty "deserve more respect and equity," backing their calls for health insurance, job security and equal pay for equal work.

source.title: Pasadena Now: Guest Opinion: Dr. Steve Gibson, We Must Support Part-Time Faculty at PCC (2022)

steve-gibson.text: Endorsed by the LA County Federation of Labor, Los Angeles County Democratic Party and Los Angeles League of Conservation Voters.

source.title: Steve Gibson for Pasadena City College (campaign site)

david-coher.text: (2020) Opposed PUSD's $500 million Measure O facilities bond, citing failed oversight of the earlier Measure TT bond and calling Measure O "a blank check for a School District in need of reform."

source.title: Pasadena Now: Guest Opinion | David Coher: No Oversight Means No on O (Oct. 2020)

david-coher.text: (2020) As a Pasadena planning commissioner, wrote that "The Pasadena Way requires us to establish a civilian oversight commission for our Police Department."

source.title: Pasadena Now: Guest Opinion | David Coher: Civilian Oversight is the Pasadena Way (June 2020)

david-coher.text: (2023) Urged the City Council to keep Pasadena Water and Power's reference resource plan and reject eliminating greenhouse emissions by 2030, calling it infeasible and saying it would cost at least $1.35 billion more.

source.title: Pasadena Now: Guest Opinion | David B. Coher: Climate Change Requires Climate Responsibility (2023)

notes: Steve Gibson: existing items kept (re-attributed where they paraphrase his campaign; 2024 item year-prefixed) plus his campaign site and op-eds.
